title: Never send the reviewer key to a base URL that is not https
spec:
Conductor sends the reviewer's API key in an Authorization header to the provider's `base_url`. Today only the setup UI refuses a non-https URL, so a hand-written conductor.toml with `http://` sends the key in clear text. Enforce the rule in two places:

1. conductor/config.py: give `Provider` a read-only property `is_https -> bool`, true when the scheme of `base_url` (parsed with `urllib.parse.urlsplit`) is exactly `https`. When a `Profile` is validated (where it already checks that every model names a known provider), raise `ConfigError` if the reviewer is a model (not `"brain"`) whose provider is not https, with the message `privacy.<profile name>: the reviewer '<reviewer>' needs an https base_url, because Conductor sends it the API key`. A `brain` reviewer needs no https provider.
2. conductor/reviewer.py: in `review`, before reading the API key, if the reviewer's provider is not https return `Verdict.failed(ModelError.of(PROVIDER_UNUSABLE, "insecure-base-url", f"refusing to send the API key to {provider.base_url}: base_url must be https"))` without calling `post`. The key must never appear in the verdict.

Add tests: a profile whose reviewer provider is http is rejected; a brain reviewer on an http provider is accepted; review() on an http provider returns that error and never calls post.
